content:
According to a recent Guardian report, Apple is participating in negotiations to bid for the U.S. broadcast rights of The Open Championship golf tournament. Netflix and Amazon are also expected to show interest in these rights.

The Open Championship was first held in Scotland in 1860 and is the oldest of the four men's major championships in golf, organised by The R&A. Americans sometimes refer to it as the "British Open" to distinguish it from the U.S. Open, which is held separately each year.

In 2017, NBC outbid ESPN with a higher offer to sign a 12-year broadcasting rights deal for The Open. These rights are also partially held by Versant, which operates Golf Channel. The R&A stated that they expect to engage in discussions with NBC and Versant, as well as other parties interested in the rights.

Today's report indicates that Apple has held "preliminary discussions" with The R&A regarding bidding for The Open's broadcast rights. The report cited a source "familiar with Apple's plans" and noted that Apple "remains committed to investing in sports broadcast rights and will continue to seek suitable sports properties."

An R&A spokesperson, responding to the Guardian, said:

"Our partnership with NBC and Versant has been outstanding, bringing significant benefits to The Open, the AIG Women's Open, and our other championships and international events. Looking ahead to the next U.S. media rights cycle for The R&A, we expect to engage with our existing partners NBC and Versant in due course. We will also continue to monitor the evolving broadcasting landscape and the broad interest from various parties in our rights."

Last year, Apple announced a major partnership with F1, becoming the exclusive broadcast partner for F1 in the United States. The company also streams Friday Night Baseball and MLS matches.
